title: Dear John by Rachel Lin at the HERE Arts Center #dearjohnplay #rachel...
transcript: Nobody likes getting a random message on Facebook, but imagine it ends up being from a long-lost parent you never knew. This new solo show by Rachel Lin weaves her mother's immigrant experience with her own coming of age story, which was complicated enough before her father started contacting her. Once he's confirmed that Rachel is his daughter, he tries to passively insert himself into her life as a father figure. Rachel recounts the next years of receiving advice-ridden letters from him, reciting each one as John, but comically assuming a different persona each time, to highlight the fact that he's still practically a stranger. She poignantly conveys this conflict between curiosity about John and the self-assurance of having made it this far in life without him. I thought the emotional impact was slightly dulled by the production being a little overstuffed and overproduced. There's a lot of busywork happening on stage which dampens the momentum, especially when there's already a lot of time jumping and context switching in the narrative. Still, Rachel deftly moves through the piece’s somewhat convoluted structure to deliver an undeniably interesting story. With that, another program for my collection.
